title: COTA founder expects $1B+ in economic impact from F1 Grand Prix

 AUSTIN, Texas — The Formula 1 United States Grand Prix returns to Circuit of the Americas (COTA) Thursday for a four-day event.
 "If we look at the total impact of tourism on Austin over the course of the year, more than 10 percent of it happens just this weekend alone. That's how big this is," said Bobby Epstein, founder and chairman at COTA.
 Epstein projects this weekend's festivities will bring in more than one billion dollars for the region from out-of-state visitors alone.
 "This weekend's race should bring well over a billion from just the out-of-state visitors, not the out-of-area visitors, actually just out-of-state. Probably close to $1.3 billion," he said.
 A sign at the South Congress Motel calls this year's F1 event at COTA 'The biggest weekend ever.' (Photo: CBS Austin/Audrey Wong) 
 RELATED | Free F1 fan experiences pop up around downtown Austin ahead of race weekend 
 Businesses like the Fairmont Austin Hotel are already taking advantage.
 "We've got our pop-up shops. We'll have a car in the lobby. We have some special events starting on Thursday," said Michael Culver, general manager at the Fairmont.
 F1 merchandise pop-ups are in the lobby at the Fairmont Austin Hotel ahead of the U.S. Grand Prix at COTA (Photo: CBS Austin/Audrey Wong) 
 "When you combine the great F1 event with the University of Texas and their big football game, and we also have the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night, it's great for the city," said Culver.
 Of the 1,048 rooms at the Fairmont, nearly all are booked over the next four days.
 "We should be sold out," said Culver. "You know, we're 1,048 guest rooms, so when you look at that, that's almost 3,000 rooms sold in one weekend."
 F1's impact has scaled over time
 "When we first started, there was a group called Formula Money that did a study and said we could have a $300 million economic impact to Austin. And we thought that was going to be great," remembered Epstein.
 In the past 15 years, Angelou reports that COTA's 15-year economic impact to the state of Texas exceeds $13.7 billion.
 In a presentation given to the Austin Tourism Commission, Angelou Economics estimated that the total expenditures at the 2024 race were around $1.1 billion. The firm estimates that around $970 million was spent during the 2025 event.\
 Circuit of The Americas now has a Texas-sized welcome for race fans: a cowboy hat Guinness World Records has certified as the world’s largest. (Photo: COTA) 
 Hritik Ghorpade, an Operations Research Analyst at Angelou who led the studies, explains that coinciding events likely play a role in the difference between 2024 and 2025.
 "The race weekends are never alike. I remember in 2024, [the] Texas Longhorns hosted Georgia for a very thrilling game the same weekend," he said. "We anticipate more of the same this weekend since Mississippi is coming to the town."
 ALSO | COTA unveils 'World's Largest Cowboy Hat' ahead of US Grand Prix 
 Angelou Economics estimates total direct, indirect, and induced spending. Ghorpade provided an example to explain the different ways money is spent for the event.
 "Let's say you buy a hot dog at COTA, [that's] direct spending, right? So indirect spending is [when] COTA has a local food vendor or local food supplier to make sure they have enough hot dogs...that business-to-business purchase is nothing but indirect impact," he said. 
 For induced spending, Ghorpade explains that the workforce will spend their wages, putting money back into the economy.
 "The local vendor or food supplier hires people to make sure everything is running well, and they get paid, and they spend their money into the economy for their family needs or for themselves," Ghorpade said.
 COTA gives fans an early start to US Grand Prix weekend with Grand Prixview Thursday 
 COTA is expecting 400,000 people on-site over the next four days. The track has also expanded its seating capacity and recently opened its new amusement park, COTALAND. Several factors considered, Ghorpade said total expenditures at this year's event could be record-breaking.
 "Considering all things, the signs are pretty good," he said.
 Impact beyond the track
 While the U.S. Grand Prix is hosted at COTA, Epstein said stakeholders throughout Austin stand to benefit from the event.
 "The 1.3 or 1.5 billion dollars that comes into the Austin economy, it's circulating through tens of thousands of different people's hands... it happens in the city throughout restaurants and hotels and shops, and that's what we're so excited about," he said.
 COTA is employing 12,000 people for the event.
 "That's everything from logistics, directional life safety, traffic, concessions, and ushers, and the list goes on and on," said Epstein. "But that's 12,000 households that this touches, just at the track."
 To put the scope of the event into perspective, Epstein said, " This is now America's biggest single weekend sporting event. There's nothing bigger. The 400-plus thousand people over the weekend and the economic impact, nothing comes close."
 Gates for the first day of events open at COTA tomorrow at 11:30 a.m., and parking opens at 11 a.m.
